prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity interaction-detail board showing TWO STATES OF THE SAME Workbench component, side by side, as crisp flat UI screenshots. This is a close-up of the approved research-program panel and its attached composer, not alternative layouts. The supplied screenshot is the exact visual and composition reference: preserve its dark restrained materials, Geist type, compact topic navigation, single focused question and shared composer. Omit unrelated app header, conversation and floating context from the close-up. Landscape board, generous readable text. Each panel shows the entire research-program/composer unit at the same scale. Thin line icons, no marketing, device frame, invented AI work or new product controls. UI in English; a small outside label marks each state. "Illustrative" outside the UI.
Interaction: Edit question. Left label "Editing Q2". Program still has four questions, Switching selected, "2 of 4". Focused saved question "What makes switching difficult?" remains displayed above. The ONE existing composer is in mode "Edit question · Q2", with Cancel. Its prefilled question has been edited to "Which integrations make switching away from CCC difficult?" Its contextual action is Save changes, not Send and not Add question. Start research remains visible but disabled while this edit is unresolved. No second textbox or modal.
Right label "After Save changes". Same panel and same four-question navigation, Switching remains selected, "2 of 4". The saved focused question is now "Which integrations make switching away from CCC difficult?" The original rationale stays unchanged: "Separate contractual participation from integrations and operating dependencies." Small confirmation "Question updated". The composer returns to its ordinary compact placeholder "Refine the framing…", with icon-only send. Start research is enabled again. The operation replaces Q2's wording; it does NOT add a fifth question, initiate research or produce an assistant response.
purpose: Detail of one previously discussed interaction, draft and applied states; not an alternative composition
